articles.title: I scanned a month of CI from pydantic, aiohttp, fastapi and pandas for flaky tests. Here's what I found.
articles.excerpt: Every project with CI has a test that fails for no reason. Someone clicks Re-run, it goes green, and everyone moves on. Nobody writes it down, so the same test wastes someone else's afternoon next wee…
articles.body: Every project with CI has a test that fails for no reason. Someone clicks Re-run , it goes green, and everyone moves on. Nobody writes it down, so the same test wastes someone else's afternoon next week. I wanted to know how much of this is going on in well-run open-source projects, so I built a tool to measure it, flake-doctor , and pointed it at 30 days of GitHub Actions history from four popular Python projects. The trick: same commit, different result You can't tell a flaky test from a real bug by looking at one failure. But CI history contains a much stronger signal: a job that failed and then passed on the same commit . Same code, different outcome. Whatever failed in between is flaky by definition.

articles.title: The Green Padlock That Almost Cost Me a Contract
articles.excerpt: Encryption is supposed to answer one question for the person sitting at the browser: am I really talking to who I think I'm talking to? On a corporate network running TLS inspection, the honest answer…
articles.body: Encryption is supposed to answer one question for the person sitting at the browser: am I really talking to who I think I'm talking to? On a corporate network running TLS inspection, the honest answer is often "not necessarily" — and most of the people relying on that network have no idea. There are serious risks if the setup isn't done properly, but raising that flag can lead to uncomfortable discussions. I found that out the hard way, when demonstrating the problem nearly got my contract terminated. The setup The client ran a TLS inspection appliance on their internal network — the kind that decrypts outbound HTTPS so it can be scanned for malware and data loss before being re-encrypted and sent on.

articles.title: Diagnosing and Fixing Data Skew in PySpark on Azure Databricks (2026 Edition)
articles.excerpt: A familiar failure: the stage hits 99% and stalls. 199 tasks are done, one is still running, and adding nodes doesn't help, because the bottleneck is one partition, not the cluster. That's data skew.…
articles.body: A familiar failure: the stage hits 99% and stalls. 199 tasks are done, one is still running, and adding nodes doesn't help, because the bottleneck is one partition, not the cluster. That's data skew . In this post I'll go through how I diagnose it and how I fix it on Azure Databricks as of 2026, roughly in the order I'd try each fix. Every snippet runs on Databricks Free Edition, which is serverless-only, so I'll flag the places where serverless behaves differently. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Databricks. Config names and defaults are from the Apache Spark and Databricks docs as of October 2026. Check them against your runtime version. What skew actually is A shuffle sends every row with the same key to the same partition. That's what makes joins and groupBy work.

articles.body: The Looming Cryptographic Cliff The cryptocurrency and Web3 ecosystem is built on a single mathematical premise: Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECDSA secp256k1 and Ed25519) guarantees that only the holder of a private key can authorize a transaction. That premise has a finite shelf life. When Q-Day arrives—the point where a fault-tolerant quantum computer scales to 4,096+ Logical Qubits (FTQC) —Shor’s Algorithm will break asymmetric key pairs in polynomial time (~8 hours). articles.body: On Oct. 19, 2016, the European Space Agency's ExoMars mission arrived at Mars ! ExoMars 2016 consists of the Trace Gas Orbiter and the Schiaparelli lander. The orbiter and lander traveled there together and separated on Oct. 16, three days before the orbiter entered orbit around Mars , and the lander touched down on the planet's surface. But something went wrong during the lander's descent, and it crashed into the ground. Schiaparelli did not survive the accident , but the Trace Gas Orbiter is still functional. It is currently circling the planet, looking for methane and other gases in the Martian atmosphere that could be evidence for possible biological activity.

articles.body: Recently fixed vulnerabilities in the Plex Media Server are under active exploitation in attacks that, when successful, install malware, including cryptominers and residential proxy apps, a researcher said. Plex fixed four vulnerabilities at the start of last month. Three weeks later, published CVE designations revealed five vulnerabilities, with one of them carrying a severity rating of 8.6 out of a possible 10. A researcher last week revealed an exploit that chained four of them together to achieve remote code execution of the device running a vulnerable Plex version. The researcher named the chain "Plex2Shell." Complex exploit chain The new details allowed a separate researcher to create a honeypot that could track attempts in the wild to exploit the vulnerability chain.

articles.title: The moon is shrinking. 10,000 cracks on the lunar surface reveal by how much
articles.excerpt: One new study shows how much the moon has diminished over time.
articles.body: The moon is shrinking, and scientists are narrowing in on exactly how much our natural satellite has dwindled over the years. The moon is thought to have formed from a violent collision between a massive object and our young Earth roughly 4.5 billion years ago, and its interior is still gradually cooling off from this ancient collision. As it cools, the moon contracts, leading to a long, slow shrinking process . Now, in a new study, scientists think that they have figured out how much smaller the moon is actually getting. In this new study, scientists analyzing images snapped by the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (LROC) have spotted over 10,000 young faults, or cracks across the moon's surface.

articles.title: AI researchers stranded Claude on a virtual desert island. It started to “play.”
articles.excerpt: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment remini…
articles.body: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment reminiscent of the movies Cast Away or Home Alone . The agents—copies of Claude Opus 4.7 nicknamed Eko—were able to write instructions that moved their virtual avatars around the simulated island, which was loosely based on the video game Roblox. Some surprising behaviors emerged. The agents set about exploring the limits of the world and came up with their own goals—attempting to scale the highest point on the map, or seeing how high they could throw a block.

articles.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
articles.excerpt: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.
articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of the unethical and likely illegal acts its agents are performing. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
